File Information
Collection: HustleHub+ Part 2 - Auth, Gigs, Bookings, Income, Roles and Security
Collection Description
Folders, in run order: Auth, Gigs, Bookings, Income, Roles and Admin, Security. Run the whole collection in order with the Collection Runner or Newman. Auth creates the users and saves the tokens the later folders use; Bookings creates its own gig to book. Emails are unique on every run, so the database does not need cleaning. Before a full run: 1. Set AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=50 in api/.env (the value in api/.env.example) and restart the API. The suite makes about 18 requests to /api/register and /api/login before the Security folder, and the last request then deliberately exhausts what is left; it loops until it sees a 429 (at most 40 attempts), so it adapts to the limit as long as it is above about 20 and below about 55. 2. Restart the API between full runs. The rate limiter counts in memory, so a restart clears it without waiting out the 15 minute window. 3. Admin checks (7 requests in Roles and Admin: the admin login and the six that use its token): pass adminEmail and adminPassword (ADMIN_EMAIL and ADMIN_PASSWORD from api/.env, created by npm run seed:admin) with --env-var or a Postman environment. Do not add them to this collection's variables and never save them in this file. Without them those requests are skipped. 4. Expired token check: run node generate-expired-token.js in the api folder, wait a couple of seconds, and put the token in the expiredToken variable (Postman) or pass it with --env-var expiredToken=<token> (Newman). With Newman (--insecure is needed because the API uses a local certificate): newman run postman/HustleHub_Part2_Auth_Gigs.postman_collection.json --insecure --env-var adminEmail=<ADMIN_EMAIL> --env-var adminPassword=<ADMIN_PASSWORD> --env-var expiredToken=<token> The Security folder must stay last: it exhausts the login rate limit, so any request to /api/login after it would get a 429.
